full_judgment: 17. In two unreported decisions of this court in Writ Petition Nos. 1776 of 2004 and 2173 of 2004 it has been held that all the share holders of a private limited company who personally guarantee loans disbursed to a limited company were held not to be defaulting borrowers খেলাপী ঋন গ্রহীতা  ) since the loan was neither obtained for themselves nor for স্বার্থ সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রতিষ্ঠান  A guarantor guarantees repayment of a loan advanced to a borrower. The primary liability for repayment lies upon the borrower and upon his failure to pay the same, the guarantor is liable to pay it. It may well be the case that an influential person of high standing guarantees the repayment of a loan obtained by his employee or some other Poor person to whom the bank is reluctant to provide credit. If the borrower in such cases defaults the guarantor is, no doubt, liable to repay the loan but it would be unfair to an innocent guarantor if his name is included in the CIB list and all banking transactions suddenly stopped. In our opinion, that could not have been the intention of the legislature. In such case no one will come forward to guarantee loan taken by a person of lesser means. In course of default if a case is filed under the Artha Rin Ain for recovery of loan amount the guarantor can be joined as a party in the suit for recovery of loan money and decree may be passed against both the borrower and the guarantor but even, according to the Artha Rin Ain, the decree can be executed against the guarantor only if it remains unsatisfied by proceedings against the principal borrower. This is to give protection to the guarantor. Similarly, if a person stands guarantee for a loan disbursed to a borrower and if the borrower fails to repay the loan within the stipulated period or even to keep up with the instalments the borrower's name may be included in the CIS list but not that of the guarantor.
